answer: Paying an examination charge of £77, charged again each time a name fails is the first step for every name, and the second step costs the same again. A seat is earned, not claimed: Elected tinsmith work permit backed by the tinsmiths society makes sure of that, since a permit smiths hold after solder audits. The numbers simply do not work for a farm, and that is the whole defence. Copying a name buys nothing here — each copy must pay the same toll again. One echo, one entry. pigment is written on the receipt. The clerk notes umber.
